VGW Brings Chumba Casino to iPhone With a New Native App

Published November 4, 2026 · 4 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

Virtual Gaming Worlds (VGW) has released a new native iOS app for Chumba Casino, giving US players full access to the sweepstakes casino's game library directly on iPhone and iPad through the Apple App Store. The company says the app carries over its entire gaming portfolio, including Social Plus titles, progressive jackpots, and live social casino games, with account balances, profiles, and game history syncing in real time between the app and Chumba's desktop site.

What the new app adds

Beyond simply bringing the game catalog to mobile, the app supports Face ID and Touch ID login and carries forward Chumba's dual-currency structure: Standard Play using Gold Coins, and Promotional Play using Sweeps Coins in the states where Chumba offers both. The app enforces the same safeguards expected of a sweepstakes casino operating in the US, including App Store age-gating for players 21 and over and mandatory identity verification before real play.

VGW's Chief Product and Revenue Officer, Scott Milford, called bringing Chumba to the App Store an important step for the brand's reach and the player experience going forward. The company plans to gradually retire its older, more limited "Chumba Lite" iOS app, which only supported Standard Play, and will notify existing Lite users with the option to move over to the full app.

The regulatory backdrop

The app launch comes a couple of months after VGW agreed, in September 2026, to pay New York Attorney General Letitia James's office $8 million to resolve an investigation into Chumba Casino, Global Poker, and Luckyland Slots. New York's AG had argued that letting players acquire Sweeps Coins — which could be redeemed for cash or prizes at roughly a coin per dollar spent — amounted to gambling with something of value under state law, which sweepstakes casinos aren't permitted to offer in New York. VGW received a cease-and-desist order in mid-2025 and stopped offering its virtual-coin model to New York players as part of that resolution; this week's app launch doesn't change that New York carve-out, since the broader legal questions around the sweepstakes-casino model are still being worked out state by state.

Why it matters to US players

Sweepstakes casinos like Chumba occupy a gray area that regulators in several states have been actively testing, and a mobile-first push like this one signals VGW is still investing in growth in the states where it continues to operate, even as it navigates restrictions elsewhere. Players outside New York gain an easier way to access the platform on iOS, but the underlying legal patchwork — different rules state by state on whether sweepstakes-style coin models are even permitted — hasn't gone away, and it's worth knowing your own state's current stance before assuming a new app means a straightforward green light everywhere.
